title: Conditional Euclidean-Hamiltonian reductions for sign-problem toy models
summary: Euclidean Monte Carlo methods are effective when the path-integral weight is real and nonnegative, but finite-density fermion systems often produce sign-changing or complex scalar weights after the fermionic sector is traced out. Hamiltonian formulations avoid this complex-weight sampling problem but face rapid Hilbert-space growth. This paper studies a conditional Euclidean-Hamiltonian (CEH) reduction that combines these two descriptions.
